clue.text: This sort of clue held by the French in game

indicators.note: something held by another piece sits within it, so one set of letters goes inside the other

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'
this clue is itself an across clue, number 1 in that direction

explanation.surface: A French puzzle-setter slips a clue into a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This sort of clue' refers to the clue itself: it is an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A field sport played with netted sticks, originally from North America, is a game.

clue.text: Randy slut upset — it's offensive to withhold love

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the word slut are knocked over and rearranged
withholding something means keeping it back, so a letter is taken out of the word for offensive

parts.note: something offensive is foul
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rude word, it is suggested, is offensive when it holds back affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SLUT into LUST; 'to withhold' takes O out of FOUL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for sexually eager, a synonym of full of desire.

clue.text: Girl in conversation with an impostor

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the girl's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Charlotte is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is chatting with a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conversation' looks like a place for the girl to sit, but it signals a sound-alike: CHARLOTTE, said aloud, gives the first seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack or fraud who pretends to skills they lack is an impostor.

clue.text: Excelled in alfresco party on Tyneside

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, out of doors
a do is a party
Tyneside, round Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Someone shone at an outdoor party in Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten or surpassed is to be bettered; excelled here is the past participle meaning outshone.

clue.text: Rugby players meeting with extremely pricey alcohol

parts.note: a scrum is a set formation where the forwards of two rugby teams bind together

indicators.note: extremely means at its extremes, so only the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Rugby players get together over very expensive drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMPY is strong rough cider from the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough farmhouse cider is an alcoholic drink, so it is a kind of alcohol.

clue.text: Take Don for granted?

parts.note: take for granted means suppose without proof, and to don is to put on, as one takes on an air; the question mark flags the word play with Don sitting inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to take a man called Don for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both 'take for granted' and 'don' (put on, as of a manner), and the clue wraps the second sense inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something without proof is to take it as given, and the same verb also means to put on.

clue.text: Get garage to change the sum total

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of get garage are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist asks a garage to amend the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole formed by adding all the parts together is an aggregate, a synonym of a total.

clue.text: Rip off fleece

definitions.meaning: to rip off is to cheat someone out of money
to fleece is to strip someone of money by trickery

explanation.definitionFit: To cheat by deception is both to rip off and to fleece someone.

clue.text: Island where Ernie for one is said to be put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upward, so the letters are turned round
is said means spoken, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: ERNIE, the Premium Bond number generator, takes its name from the initials of Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment

explanation.surface: Someone named Ernie is reported to have been given lodging on a Mediterranean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks British Premium Bond winners. ACRONYM said aloud can be spelt ACRONIM, and 'put up' turns that into the island.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, also called Menorca, is an island.

clue.text: Head of school, being important, shows a little knowledge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: mattering means being important

explanation.surface: A headteacher who thinks highly of himself reveals how little he knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of school' tempts as a person; it gives only the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, superficial acquaintance with a subject is a smattering, a small amount of knowledge.

clue.text: Girl heading off for island

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: Fiona is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman sets out for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean isle with a famous abbey is an island.

clue.text: Editor's injunction to readers to play the game

definitions.meaning: a newspaper's leader is its editorial column, so an editor could urge readers to go along with it
a children's game in which everyone copies the one in front

explanation.surface: An editor tells readers to toe the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper's leader is its editorial, so the phrase is an editor's request to agree with the paper's line, and also the name of a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which players copy whatever the one in front does is a game.

clue.text: Let tyro perhaps try his luck here

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of let tyro may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A novice is invited to have a flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw of tickets for prizes is a place of pure chance, where anyone may chance his luck.

clue.text: Small boarder finds black bird with lots of eggs

parts.note: a rook is a black bird of the crow family
spawn is the mass of eggs laid by fish or frogs

explanation.surface: A tiny lodger discovers a crow with a huge clutch of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarder' is a cryptic word for a chess piece on a board; the answer is ROOK'S PAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: On the chessboard a pawn is the humblest piece, so the one in front of a rook is a small piece on the board.

clue.text: Way of thinking after a lawyer's opening

parts.note: later means after

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

explanation.surface: A thought comes once the lawyer has opened the case.
explanation.walkthrough: LATERAL thinking means solving problems by indirect, creative routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways, indirect reasoning is called lateral thinking, so the word names a way of thinking.

clue.text: Hindering the conductor as train sets minute, off

indicators.note: off says the letters of train sets are put out of order

explanation.surface: A guard is held up as the train pulls away a minute late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a train guard; here it is an electrical conductor. The word 'minute' plays no part in the wordplay and only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing the flow of an electric current is resisting it, as a resistor hinders a conductor.

clue.text: The armoury is in a mess

definitions.meaning: a room where guns are stored
the junior officers' dining room on a warship

explanation.definitionFit: A store for firearms and a junior officers' mess on a naval ship both share this name.

clue.text: Crank urged on to stand

indicators.note: to crank something is to turn it, so the letters of urged on are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An eccentric is spurred to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand pain or treatment is to bear or experience it, a synonym of go through.

clue.text: Speak very rapidly and stagger away 23,018 ar

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
off means away

explanation.surface: Someone gabbles and lurches off.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue ends in stray text from the page ('23,018 ar'), which is no part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a long list fluently and fast is to rattle it off, speaking quickly.

clue.text: Sea off America with singular jellyfish

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the USA is America
S is the abbreviation for singular in grammar

explanation.surface: A stretch of ocean off the American coast holds one odd jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusas are the free-swimming bell-shaped stage of creatures like jellyfish.

clue.text: Mother carrying topi for Gandhi, for example, example

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a topi is a sun helmet, a hat

explanation.surface: A mother wears a pith helmet for the Indian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue repeats 'example' by a reading slip. MAHATMA, 'great soul', was the title given to Gandhi.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title of reverence for a great sage, famously held by Gandhi.

clue.text: Late watch for marksman

parts.note: the late person is dead
to eye is to watch

explanation.surface: A sniper keeps an eye out late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is a very accurate shooter, an expert marksman.

clue.text: A little fossil, very lustrous white

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small fossil has a shining pale sheen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with the shine and pale colour of silver is lustrous and whitish.

clue.text: Strip show doesn't need such practice

definitions.text: Strip show doesn't need such practice

parts.words: Strip show doesn't need such practice
parts.note: a striptease has no use for a costumed run-through, since its performers end up without costumes

explanation.definitionFit: A final full-costume run-through before opening night is a theatrical practice.

clue.text: Drive from British port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A motorist sets out from a British harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour and energy, a synonym of drive in the sense of dynamism.

clue.text: In any event everyone is in uniform

definitions.meaning: everyone looks identical when dressed alike

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless, and also describes everyone being identical, as people in uniform are.

clue.text: Brainbox put away in asylum

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: loony bin is slang for a mental asylum
off means away

explanation.surface: A genius is committed to a mental hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist or clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is a very clever person, and a boffin is a scientific expert or egghead.

clue.text: Get a pain in the neck in attempt to exhibit wall-hanging

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a pest is an annoying person, a pain in the neck

explanation.surface: Someone gets a crick while trying to put up a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile picture, typically hung on a wall.
